title: Offline Sovereign Agent Fast-Boot & Protocol 128 Local Verification via Apple MLX Engine
target_platform: Apple Silicon M1 (16GB Unified Memory) via Apple MLX (mlx-lm)
hypothesis: Embedding cached mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-4bit into a local Python runner within plugins/sanctuary-core enables autonomous offline execution of Protocol 128 code audits and Pre-Completion Verification Gates in < 3 seconds with 0 cloud tokens.
falsification_criteria: Local MLX Python runner exceeds 5.5 GB RAM during AST verification or requires external internet/cloud API connectivity to resolve dependencies.

evidence.details: Engineered forge_llm.py with dual-mode MLX runner (persistent server HTTP vs one-shot CLI execution) and Ollama fallback.
Tested forge_llm.py query: Output 'The capital of France is Paris.' Speed: 7.89 tok/sec. Peak memory: 4.431 GB.
Tested forge_llm.py verify: Generated valid JSON Pre-Completion Gate response with PASS. Prompt throughput: 83.681 tok/sec. Peak memory: 4.443 GB (< 5.5 GB falsification threshold passed).

lessons_learned: Auto-detecting sys.platform == 'darwin' and checking local HTTP server readiness allows instantaneous queries when server is live without sacrificing one-shot CLI fallback.
Prompt processing speeds on M1 Metal hit 83.7 tok/sec for structured JSON schema validation.
First 20 lines coding convention and dual-mode query interface ensure smooth subagent and tool invocation across the sanctuary ecosystem.
